x.around: As evening approaches, the price will go up (around $5 for a medium trip). After dark, most of the taxis disappear. However, there are usually ones waiting outside expat bars, which will ask at least $10, even for short trips. You can also call a night service (if you can find a current number for one).

hidden.d: Aka Backside Beach. The beach directly behind the Jesus statue, it's a scenic, inverted c-shaped coastline with near-transparent waters much better than the one at Areia Branca.

The statue of Jesus that stands on a headland to the east of Dili. Rumour has it that, when the mainly Muslim Indonesians built the statue as a gift to the mainly Christian Timorese, they designed it so that Jesus would be facing…
Learn about the struggle for Timor-Leste's independence and what the people went through in the massive 25-year-long struggle.

A memorial to Sparrow Force, an Australian unit that fought the Japanese in Timor for several years, plus an exhibition on the unit and on the Timorese experience of the war. Good views over Dili and a café open on weekends.
Set in a prison used during Portuguese and Indonesian times, you can visit the dark cells in which prisoners were held.

x.intro: Dili is the capital city of Timor-Leste and its largest city. It is squeezed along the narrow plains between Timor's northern coast and the central mountains which run the length of the island.

must.d: Site of the Santa Cruz massacre on 12 November 1991 when at least 250 Timorese were murdered after a funeral procession for activist Sebastião Gomes, who was shot in Motael Church.
The oldest church in Timor-Leste. Originally from around 1800, the current building dates to 1955. The church played an important role in the independence struggle.

n.es: Iglesia de San Antonio de Motael

and Maubara are less than an hour west along the coast road (make sure to turn right at the T-junction in Tibar).
is suitable for a day trip, especially if you want to see some mountains while staying on decent roads. Head west from Dili and go straight at the Tibar T-junction.

x.safe: Dili has a problem with phone and bag snatching. Be careful when walking along the street, as scooter riders may grab your phone or bag right out of your hands. Likewise be careful if you are on a motorbike with your phone exposed, particularly when moving slowly in traffic.

cities.d: the second largest city, known for its colonial architecture

x.around: Some taxis shuttle passengers around the city for US$1 (although locals pay less). Further journeys, such as to Manatuto will cost more.

hidden.d: Visit the convent mission for a look at the valuable work the sisters are doing with the children and less fortunate of Baucau. They also have a small store with local handicrafts.
A large spring-fed pool owned by the Pousada, set in lush grounds, with a diving board and a slide. Beautiful place for a swim.
Take a walk around the colonial centre of town. The abandoned and often scorched buildings are eerie reminders of a bygone era.
Beautiful and popular white sand beach with bungalows and camping.

x.intro: Baucau is Timor-Leste's second largest city, behind Dili. It is located near the northern coast of Timor-Leste, 130 km east of Dili. Baucau is an important administrative and agricultural centre. It is the capital of a district with the same name.

cities.d: the once-former capital of the Timor-Leste community is situated in one of Timor's most beautiful highlands

x.intro: Ermera is in East Timor. The once-former capital of the East Timorese community is situated in one of Timor's most beautiful highlands.

cities.d: the capital of the Ermera District situated in a beautiful valley
a small district just to the west of Dili

x.around: Just east of Liquiçá are the ruins of Aipelo Prison, where the Portuguese kept rebellious Timorese kings. Placards amid the ruins tell the story.

cities.d: Timor-Leste's third largest city near the eastern Indonesian border

x.around: The highway runs northwest–southeast and intersects with Maliana's main street next to the sports field and gymnasium. This area is easy to walk around, but some hotels are on a hill that is accessed by a road turning right off the highway about 500 metres south past the intersection (opposite a cemetery).
x.intro: Maliana is the third-largest city in Timor-Leste and has the air of a dusty wild west town. There's not much in the town, but it is surrounded by interesting landscapes and can make a good stopover or base for daytrips.

cities.d: contains many traditional fishing villages dating back to Portuguese colonial times

hidden.d: Just about completed, this is the most striking building in Suai and replaces the one that was destroyed in the 1999 massacre by pro-Indonesian militiamen.

x.intro: Suai is in East Timor. Near the coast, the sleepy town of 10,000 people (2015) boasts beaches and traditional fishing villages dating back to Portuguese colonial times.

intro: The Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste, commonly known as Timor-Leste (Tetum: Timór Lorosa'e) or East Timor, is one of the world's newest countries: after a long struggle, it gained independence from Indonesia in 2002 and is now an off-the-beaten-path destination for diving and adventure. A former Portuguese colony, it is one of only two countries in Asia with a Roman Catholic majority, the other one being the Philippines.
